author: Dale Philip
description:
I finally left North Jakarta, switching my $40 budget hotel there for a more luxury $200 hotel in Jakarta's south.

The budget hotel I stayed in was the Holiday Inn Express, which is connected to the Emporium Pluit Mall. It was very basic but in my opinion was pretty good value at just $40 a night, when you consider that it includes breakfast and comes with the convenience of being able to come and go from the mall so easily.

I was eating my meals in that mall every day, and on my final day I visited 'Taliwang Bali' a Balinese chain restaurant that I'd been meaning to try for a while. I tried their signature 'Nasi Bali Mbok Jegeg' which is a platter of all sorts of food, and I enjoyed the variety of that.

I'd never visited South Jakarta in my past trips, but knew it was the most upmarket area of the city, with loads of nice hotels, condominiums and a central business district where the country's biggest companies have their HQs.

author: Dale Philip
description: I visited Mack's Creamery in the Blok M area of South Jakarta. They have all sorts of weird ice cream flavours and most of them tasted surprisingly good.
title: Beef Ice Cream in Jakarta, Indonesia 🇮🇩

author: Dale Philip
description:
I visited Uma Oma Cafe in the Blok M area of South Jakarta. Their concept is of recreating the comforting feeling of visiting your grandmother's house, with traditional Indonesian home-cooked comfort food and vintage interior / vibe.

The Bebek Goreng there was very tasty but there wasn't much meat on the portion of duck so I left still feeling hungry.
title: Fried Duck Meal in Jakarta, Indonesia 🇮🇩
